## Page 15

C O M P U T A T I O N A L  S E M A N T I C S A C T  I I  — W H Y  T H I S  A R C H I T E C T U R E  E X I S T S
Not the truth of a claim — its admissibility under a horizon.
AOSP does not compute whether a claim is true (Rice/Gödel forbid that in general). It computes a decidable, restricted question: in what epistemic state is the claim, relative to a 
declared horizon.
THE HORIZON
H = ⟨ S, Σ, T, R, M, V ⟩
S sources — typed admitted evidence
Σ scope — declared perimeter
T transmissions — admissible transforms
R receipts — receipt + readback + hash
M matrix — support / contradiction state
V validation — false-green predicate
⟦c⟧ computes one of
• supported — backed in S within Σ, receipted in R, no conflict in 
M, V holds
• unsupported — no support within Σ
• contradiction — M holds divergent evidence
• out-of-scope — support falls outside Σ
• review-required — V not yet satisfied
• blocking-debt — a transform in T lacks receipt in R
Changing the horizon can change the state — that tracked relativity is what makes it computable.

## Page 55

A P P E N D I X  A 9 D A T A  R O O M
Computational semantics — the formal object.
Why the term is defensible: the object of computation is a total function into a finite, discrete set of states — decidable by construction within a declared 
horizon.
The semantic function
⟦c⟧ₕ : Claim × Horizon → { supported, unsupported, contradiction, out-of-scope, review-required, blocking-debt }     
with     H = ⟨ S, Σ, T, R, M, V ⟩
STATE CONDITIONS
• supported ⇔ ∃ support in S within Σ, reached by T, each with receipt in R, no 
conflict in M, V satisfied
• contradiction ⇔ M holds divergent evidence
• out-of-scope / review-required ⇔ support outside Σ / V unmet
EPISTEMIC DEBT (the passive side)
debt(c,H) = { t ∈ T : receipt(t) ∉ R  ∨ ¬V(t) }
A transformation that moved meaning without sufficient receipt or validation. When 
debt(c,H) ≠ ∅ and touches c, the state is blocking-debt. This is double-entry applied to 
meaning.
Horizon relativity
⟦c⟧ₕ ≠ ⟦c⟧ₕ′ is expected: narrowing Σ, enriching S, or adding receipts in R can move a claim from review-required to supported. 
Universal truth is not horizon-relative; admissibility is — by definition. The two-node statement (Lᵢ, Lⱼ, Tᵢⱼ) is the special case of 
this structure.
